newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica maize millers prepare for possible El Nino.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica maize millers prepare for possible El Nino.

text.p: South African maize millers said on Wednesday they had begun entering into forward contracts for next season earlier than usual as the rapid build-up of the El Nino weather system raised fears of a drought.

Hamish McBain, a director at Tiger Oats, one of South Africa's biggest milling firms told Reuters the company had started developing its crop position some six weeks ago in anticipation of a shortfall next year.
"The indications are that there will be a drought. We expect a crop of between 4.5 and five million tonnes compared to consumption of between 6.5 and 7.0 million," McBain said.
"We have therefore been developing our position earlier than usual," he added.

Global weather experts have warned about the fast and intense development this year of the El Nino system, sparking fears that it could rival this century's worst occurrence of 1982/83 which caused hurricanes, droughts, fires and flooding in over 15 countries.

Produced by a disruption in the atmospheric system leading to changes in wind patterns and higher water temperatures in the Pacific, El Nino is expected to peak in December -- causing very dry weather two months into South Africa's planting season.
Steven Brenner of Brenner Mills said that as December approached, the maize milling firm might enter into more forward contracts than usual depending on the progress of El Nino and price levels.
"But there is no reason right now for panic," he added.
Two years of soaking rains have produced bumper harvests throughout southern Africa.
South Africa is forecast to harvest a commercial maize crop of 7.966 million tonnes this year, which although well below last year's is still 1 -1/2 to two million tonnes in surplus.
